statement: The function returns a result r, and r = true if and only if there exists a sequence p of length numCourses such that (1) p is a permutation of {0, 1, ..., numCourses-1}, meaning every course label in that range occurs exactly once in p, and (2) for every i with 0 <= i < len(prerequisites), letting a = prerequisites[i][0] and b = prerequisites[i][1], the unique index j_b with p[j_b] = b is strictly less than the unique index j_a with p[j_a] = a (so prerequisite b is taken before course a).
preconditions: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; 0 <= len(prerequisites) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(prerequisites), len(prerequisites[i]) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(prerequisites), 0 <= prerequisites[i][0] < numCourses and 0 <= prerequisites[i][1] < numCourses; all pairs prerequisites[i] are distinct.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r (it does not fail).
preconditions: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; 0 <= len(prerequisites) <= 5000; for every i with 0 <= i < len(prerequisites), len(prerequisites[i]) = 2; for every i with 0 <= i < len(prerequisites), 0 <= prerequisites[i][0] < numCourses and 0 <= prerequisites[i][1] < numCourses; all pairs prerequisites[i] are distinct.

statement: Let r_P be the result of can_finish(numCourses, P) and r_Q the result of can_finish(numCourses, Q). Both calls return results, and r_P = r_Q.
preconditions: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; P and Q are two lists of pairs such that each of P and Q satisfies: 0 <= len <= 5000, each element has length 2, all entries are in [0,numCourses), and all pairs are distinct; and Q is a reordering of P (Q is obtained by permuting the elements of P).

statement: Define Pπ to be the list of the same length as P whose i-th element is [π(P[i][0]), π(P[i][1])]. Let r be the result of can_finish(numCourses, P) and r' the result of can_finish(numCourses, Pπ). Both calls return results, and r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; P is a valid prerequisite list for numCourses: 0 <= len(P) <= 5000, each element has length 2, all entries are in [0,numCourses), and all pairs are distinct; π is a bijection from {0,...,numCourses-1} to itself.

statement: Let r be the result of can_finish(n, P) and r' the result of can_finish(n+1, P). Both calls return results, and r = r'.
preconditions: 1 <= n < 2000; P is a valid prerequisite list for n: 0 <= len(P) <= 5000, each element has length 2, all entries are in [0,n), and all pairs are distinct.

statement: Let r_P be the result of can_finish(numCourses, P) and r_Q the result of can_finish(numCourses, Q). Both calls return results, and if r_Q = true then r_P = true.
preconditions: 1 <= numCourses <= 2000; P and Q are valid prerequisite lists for numCourses (each has 0 <= len <= 5000, each element has length 2, all entries are in [0,numCourses), and all pairs are distinct); every pair that occurs in P also occurs in Q.
